description:
FOUND s493 (Fable, 2026-09-20).  Nobody had ever walked perl's own function index: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/angles/perlfunc-index.pl lists every `=item` of perlfunc with no p-/pl- definition in cl/ (84 of 255 names; most are keywords the compiler handles), and the real functions among them were probed one program each (angles/perlfunc/pf-*.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs main).  Each of these is `Undefined subroutine &main::NAME called` at run time -- LOUD, the program dies:

    telldir / seekdir        pf-dirpos    (rewinddir, readdir, opendir exist)
    gethostbyname / gethostbyaddr   pf-gethost   (Socket's inet_aton/inet_ntoa exist; every "resolve this host" script)
    getservbyname / getservbyport   pf-getsrv    (getprotobyname exists, via /etc/protocols -- the same approach over /etc/services)
    setpriority              pf-priority  (getpriority exists; getppid, getpgrp fine)
    formline + $^A           pf-formline  (`format`/`write` are RULED not-supported, not-supported.md §format; formline is the FUNCTION and is what swrite()-style code and some modules call -- decide whether it follows the ruling or gets a small implementation)
    untested from the static list, worth one probe each before closing this task: chroot, dbmopen/dbmclose (RULE OUT), dump (RULE OUT), ioctl, lstat-on-handle, readpipe (works), msg*/sem*/shm* (RULE OUT, cite SysV IPC), syscall (RULE OUT), sethostent & co, getnetby*, endservent & co.
Layer (9a): these are CORE builtins => cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, exported, in `known_no_of_params` if missing.  Rule 12: what is ruled out gets a not-supported.md line and a perl-shaped die ("The NAME function is unimplemented" is perl's own text on platforms lacking one), never a silent stub.
THE INSTRUMENT (keep it): the same walk over perlvar (every special variable), perlop (every operator), perlre (every construct), perlrun (every switch -- see #2097), sprintf/pack letters, and -X filetests is the rest of "the index battery"; perlfunc alone found 8 gaps in 19 probes.


=== DONE (s495f, 2026-09-25) ===
SHIPPED (runtime, cl/pcl-runtime.lisp; names registered in Config known_no_of_params, ExprToCL %RUNTIME_NAMES + %WANTARRAY_SENSITIVE, Manifest, the export list, tools/ir-inventory.pl):
  telldir / seekdir -- opendir already MATERIALISES the entry list with an index (the `(index . names)` cons), so the position IS that index; seekdir clamps; a closed/unopened handle is undef + $! EBADF on both (probed).  perl's telldir is an opaque cookie, so only the seekdir round trip is compared -- the NUMBER differs from perl's by design.
  gethostbyname / gethostbyaddr / gethostent / sethostent / endhostent -- through the C library's own gethostbyname(3)/gethostbyaddr(3)/gethostent(3) via sb-alien (struct hostent is POSIX), so the answers agree with perl's BY CONSTRUCTION, /etc/hosts quirks included (glibc maps `::1 ip6-localhost` to 127.0.0.1 in gethostent -- perl and PCL both print it).  List (name, aliases, addrtype, length, @addrs) and scalar (packed first address / the name) contexts.  lib/Socket.pm's inet_aton now resolves any non-dotted name through the core gethostbyname (it used to special-case the literal "localhost" and answer undef for every other name -- `inet_aton("bernpad")` was undef, perl 127.0.1.1).
  getservbyname / getservbyport / getservent / setservent / endservent -- the getprotobyname approach over /etc/services, ONE field reader (%p-etc-db-fields) shared with /etc/protocols, and ONE return-shape helper (%p-ent-answer) shared by every get*by*/get*ent builtin.  Exact-case names and protocols, an empty/undef proto matches any (probed), the port in host order.
  getprotoent / setprotoent / endprotoent -- file-order iteration over the protocols list.
  getnetbyname / getnetbyaddr / getnetent / setnetent / endnetent -- libc, like the host family.
  setpriority -- setpriority(2) via sb-alien beside getpriority; 1 / 0 + $! (EACCES lowering unprivileged, EINVAL bad WHICH -- probed).
  PLATFORM SYMBOLS (libc, via sb-alien): gethostbyname gethostbyaddr gethostent sethostent endhostent getnetbyname getnetbyaddr getnetent setnetent endnetent setpriority.  macOS NOT TESTED (#2196); all are POSIX, and struct hostent/netent have the same field order there.
FORMLINE -- SIZED, NOT SHIPPED (the brief's rule: nothing partial).  The full picture language (justify fields, numeric @##.## / @0##, @* / ^*, ^<<< continuation which CHOPS the caller's variable -- the args must arrive as places --, ~ / ~~, `...`, $: breaking) is more than one agent-hour against perl-probed rows.  formline now DIES "PCL: formline (format/write report formatting) is not supported" (one trappable line): its product $^A is a VALUE the program reads, so rule 12's value boundary says die, not announce (the brief said "announce"; the s329 boundary decides).  not-supported.md's format section names formline + $^A and carries the sizing.  Lifting the `format` ruling on top would additionally need per-filehandle $~ $^ $= $- $% state and `write` emitting through it.
RULED OUT (one probe each, scratch/s495f/p-static.pl): chroot, dbmopen/dbmclose, dump, ioctl, syscall, msg*/sem*/shm* -- each lives in perl and dies loudly in PCL (`Undefined subroutine &main::NAME called`); new not-supported.md section "Builtins ruled out".  `dump` deliberately NOT made a runtime name: `use Data::Dump qw(dump); dump($x)` must keep reaching the import.  lstat on a handle and readpipe WORK.
Guard: Pl/t/perlfunc-db-01.t (6 rows, 5 differential vs perl on the same machine + the formline die), inverse-verified on a 3d9b3712 extraction (6/6 fail).  everyday: index/dirpos, index/gethost, index/getsrv, index/priority -> same (rows edited out); index/formline re-pointed at the format anchor.


=== ADDENDUM (s495f, companion leg) ===
t/op/ver.t "Non-bytes leak to gethostbyaddr" (was a SKIP while gethostbyaddr did not exist) showed perl dies "Wide character in NAME" for every host/service/protocol/network lookup given a char > 0xFF (probed all six); %p-db-bytes does that now (guard row 7 of Pl/t/perlfunc-db-01.t).  op/ver.t back to its snapshot 47/7.
subject: The perlfunc INDEX, enumerated for the first time: builtins that DO NOT EXIST in PCL -- telldir/seekdir, gethostbyname/gethostbyaddr (+ the get*ent family), getservbyname/getservbyport, setpriority, formline + $^A; (flock = #2081)
